method: Static execution-path analysis; isolated QuickJS string-table computation; MSI database and managed IL decoding; Rizin; signature verification; forager reference recovery. Malware and browser application were not executed.

evidence: Godelich takes every fifth character, starting at index 4, to reconstruct cmd.exe, PowerShell paths and WMI class names. CPU AddressWidth selects System32 or SysWOW64 PowerShell. Ready-drive free space is enumerated before setup.

WMI ProcessStartup sets ShowWindow=0. EnvironmentVariables supplies SystemRoot and variables carrying the fragmented PowerShell source and executable path. Win32_Process.Create runs a reconstructed cmd.exe command that echoes the escaped source to PowerShell stdin.

The arithmetic decoder subtracts repeating Unspliced158 bytes to recover iex and the Base64 decoder. The next decoder XORs Base64-decoded strings using (a -bor b) - (a -band b), reconstructs strings and optionally invokes iex through an alias.

Msxml2.ServerXMLHTTP.6.0 performs GET to the Google Drive uc endpoint for file 1qet7Rf8kCzW3McWFZyC09p7-TRubMYAj, setting a Firefox User-Agent. A successful response is written to HKCU:\Hodder\Linket127, value Frugtavleres. The script retries until the registry key exists, then reads and Base64-decodes it.
The decoded response slice at offset 137619, length 34369, is evaluated. forager recovered the live response (171988 decoded bytes), and the slice was independently decoded for analysis.
Recovered PowerShell uses Reflection.Emit to define P/Invoke methods, hides its console through ShowWindow, and restores process environment variables from a token-derived environment block.

The recovered loader resolves VirtualAlloc, NtProtectVirtualMemory and CallWindowProcA, copies 8593 response bytes to an executable allocation, copies another response segment into a second allocation, and transfers execution through CallWindowProcA with the allocations as code and argument.

Rizin inspection of the native prefix confirms short jumps skipping padding; final native payload and runtime success were not established. No particular injected process, stealer, persistence mechanism or final C2 is asserted.
PKCS7 signature-comment certificate is self-issued: C=FR/O=Ferskvandene/CN=Ferskvandene. A signature-block comment is not evidence of a trusted publisher; its accurate presence trait is retained.
samples.coverage_gap: Original-source automatic analysis does not fully reconstruct the keyed PowerShell and remote native stage. Two suspicious traits now describe distinct supported results: concealed strided reconstruction with startup-environment transport, and hidden WMI execution of a constructed command. No sample-specific encoded constants or duplicate hostile rules were added to inflate coverage. Analyzer records flow-query-incomplete.

evidence: Tarball contains package.json and index.svg only. Manifest main points to index.svg; no lifecycle scripts or dependencies are declared. No Node installation hook or OS execution path was found.
Decoded the rotated, lower-first Base64 string table in isolated QuickJS, evaluating only decoder definitions and table rotation. The SVG hosts XHTML, loading UI and theme video.
On a secure HTTP origin, attempts to register local updater.js and handles progress, ready and failure messages. Reset unregisters origin service workers, deletes caches, then reloads.

Fallback probes CDN mirrors with fetch(cache=no-store, credentials=omit), aborts losing requests after success, and opens the selected SVG in an iframe with location.hash appended. postMessage handling checks event.source against the iframe before accepting a tab-title update.
Iframe allow attributes delegate clipboard, camera, microphone, display capture, fullscreen and other browser features. These are delegated permissions, not observed capture or exfiltration.

Fetched current achroma-ubg/svg index.svg and main repository archive with forager. Remote index renders a school-district decoy and, after 500ms, replaces it with app.svg and activates its scripts. app.svg loads achroma.js.

Deobfuscated achroma.js string table. Inspected paths initialize a browser relay engine and createFrame navigation, register agent.js, and use WebSocket relay fallbacks. Repository includes games, music, movies, chat, account and settings UI. agent.js imports the relay service worker and blocks advertising domains. No credential theft, host process execution or malware payload was established.

Recovered and inspected core/sw.js, core/api.js, core/inject.js and net/runtime.js from the referenced relay engine, plus the engine repository including its WebAssembly assets and EpoxyTransport wrapper. Service-worker route(event) selects a registered proxy tab and forwards method/body/headers to that tab over MessagePort RPC; the controller calls the configured transport and synchronizes its own cookie jar. Runtime wraps fetch/WebSocket/DOM navigation and rewrites proxied HTML/JavaScript. Engine README identifies it as a refactored Scramjet for bypassing filters. These paths support the browser-proxy purpose; no independent secret-harvesting or OS execution path was established.
samples.source_label_rationale: Script-bearing SVG, obfuscation, classroom/IXL camouflage, service workers and mirror/proxy infrastructure explain why a malware feed might collect it. The observed function is a dual-use browser proxy/games portal; camouflage alone does not establish credential phishing or host compromise.
limits: Remote references are mutable; current fetched content cannot prove historical content at publication.
updater.js is not shipped in the tarball; bikesense.org/updater.js returned 404. The actual service-worker URL depends on an unspecified embedding origin. Package fallback path was traced.

evidence: osslsigncode verifies DigitalSignature, MsiDigitalSignatureEx, certificate chain and CRL and reports Succeeded. Signer is ConnectWise, LLC, issued by DigiCert Trusted G4 Code Signing RSA4096 SHA384 2021 CA1. No timestamp is present.

Decoded string pool and column-major MSI tables. Product and service name are ScreenConnect Client (cd32b75fc727b833), version 26.6.6.9747. Service parameters and system.config pin instance-pkp9kl-relay.screenconnect.com:443 with an RSA key.

ServiceInstall specifies an automatic own-process service (type 16, start 2) with default LocalSystem account. Installer writes its URI handler, SafeBoot networking service configuration, LSA authentication package and credential-provider registrations, then installs/starts the service.

Extracted the WiX SfxCA managed cabinet and inspected IL of FixupServiceArguments, CheckMsiFileName, CheckMsiMotw and TerminateProcesses. Actions merge configured/previous service parameters, check materially renamed installers, report origin metadata and terminate ScreenConnect helper processes during uninstall. No added script/downloader custom action was found.

Client-service ProcessMessage routes clipboard, credential, transfer, command, capture and session messages. TryRunCommandMessageCommand passes received text, interpreter and time limit to the runner and returns its text result. These are expected remote-support capabilities; all dual-use detections are retained.

Package contains expected ScreenConnect assemblies/executables, authentication/credential components, native codec resources and WiX libraries. 7z reported a resource-member checksum error and cabinet tail; executable components and managed actions were recoverable, and the outer customized MSI signature verifies.
samples.source_label_rationale: Unattended privileged remote access, command execution, file transfer and credential handling explain sandbox suspicion and malware-corpus collection. ScreenConnect can be abused through an attacker-owned tenant; this artifact supplies neither proof of a hostile tenant nor unauthorized deployment or an added malware payload.
limits: Tenant ownership, installation consent and deployment provenance are unknown. BENIGN describes the inspected signed RMM artifact and does not certify its use on a host.
Supplied public Triage and Bazaar pages were inaccessible through the web tool; no incident context was invented.

corrections: Fixed-position CSS plus a 100% dimension does not identify the SVG root or establish smuggling. Removed inherited attack mapping from this neutral UI observation.
fetch() belongs with HTTP-client resource capabilities, not data formatting.
Root dimensions, viewport-meta presence and inline-script presence are markup properties. A viewport meta alone does not establish a mobile target.
rule_changes.preservation: Moved atoms retain matchers, types, platforms, exclusions and criticalities. Explicit consumers were retargeted. Exact and ancestor selectors were audited across all four tiers. Broad hosts-sinkhole and CrystalX C2 selectors no longer admit neutral CSS as an attacker fact or suppression; no neutral alias remains in objectives.

verification.focused: 31 assertions passed across 11 controls. Covers same-index strided reconstruction, sequential/wide/different-index near misses, commented assignment, environment reads, neutral SVG layout/fetch, and existing remote.svg/function.svg consumers.
verification.sample_comparison: Zero findings lost or demoted across all three original inputs and their analyzed members (1 JS, 4 npm/registry, 37 MSI units), after mapping the five relocation IDs.
verification.outside_batch: Compared original HEAD and edited rules on 14 controls, including three real SVG assets extracted from Ledger Live 4.17.0 sample 0e6bb27faf2d. Every notable-or-higher observation retained at identical severity.

low_tier_presentation_loss.reason: On the tiny environment-assignment control only, new notable behavior causes the engine to omit unreferenced baseline metadata from rendered findings. No matcher was removed; no attack detection was lost. Original batch sample findings all remain.

verification.tooling: Installed atomscan validator rejects the documented 101-rule metadata/file/naming allowance. Before/after analysis used CLEAVE_VALIDATE=0, with update, reference following and upload disabled. Final validation uses the available newer cleave binary that recognizes the reviewed allowance; no rule budget was changed. Atomscan warns that feature spec v18 is older than extractor v19.

remaining_disagreements: External malware labels disagree with BENIGN verdicts for the browser portal and intact signed RMM; supporting evidence and context gaps are recorded above.

Loader is MALICIOUS from recovered execution paths. Model probability rises from 0.92472297 to 0.98898166, but both reports have ml.lvl=-1 and model cls=0. Calibrated ML admission remains a gap; original-source automatic decoding also misses the full remote native chain.
